Rashi on Niddah 2b:15:1.english: And [the Gemara] raises a contradiction between the barrel and the ritual bath - For in both of them, there are two impairments.

Rashi on Niddah 2b:15:2.hebrew: מאי שנא - במקוה דמחזקינן למפרע טומאת ודאי, ומ"ש בחבית דקאמר ספק:
Rashi on Niddah 2b:15:2.english: What is different - In the case of the ritual bath, where we presume definite impurity retroactively, and what is different in the case of the barrel, where [the mishna] says [it is] uncertain?

Rashi on Niddah 2b:18:1.english: In the private domain, they suspend - The reason is explained later.

Rashi on Niddah 2b:1:1.hebrew: כיון דמגופה קחזיא - מועדה ועלולה היא לכך, אין לה חזקת טהרה:
Rashi on Niddah 2b:1:1.english: Since she sees [blood] from her body - She is prone and predisposed to this; [therefore,] she has no presumption of ritual purity.

Rashi on Niddah 2b:2:1.english: And how is it different from a mikveh - [The Gemara] poses the objection against both of them.

Rashi on Niddah 2b:2:2.english: That were prepared upon it - Pure items that were handled with vessels that were immersed in it.

Rashi on Niddah 2b:2:3.hebrew: בין בר"ה בין ברה"י - בין שהמקוה עומד בר"ה, דקיימא לן: ספק טומאה בר"ה ספקו טהור — הכא טמא, דלאו ספק הוא אלא ודאי, כדמפרש טעמא לקמן בשמעתין:
Rashi on Niddah 2b:2:3.english: Whether in the public domain or in the private domain - Whether the mikveh stands in the public domain—where we maintain [that regarding] an uncertainty of ritual impurity in the public domain, its uncertainty is pure—here it is impure, because it is not an uncertainty, but rather a certainty, as [the Gemara] explains the reason later in our discussion.

Rashi on Niddah 2b:3:1.hebrew: לשמאי קשיא למפרע - דהא מטמאינן טהרות למפרע, ולא אמרינן העמד מקוה על חזקתו:
Rashi on Niddah 2b:3:1.english: According to Shammai, it is difficult retroactively - For we deem pure items impure retroactively, and we do not say: "Establish the mikveh on its presumptive status."

Rashi on Niddah 2b:4:1.hebrew: דאילו מעת לעת - טהרות דמטמאין להו משום ספקא דמעת לעת לרבנן, וה"ה מפקידה לפקידה דהלל:
Rashi on Niddah 2b:4:1.english: For whereas a twenty-four-hour period - [This refers to the] ritually pure items that they deem impure due to the uncertainty of a twenty-four-hour period according to the Rabbis, and the same applies to "from examination to examination" of Hillel.

Rashi on Niddah 2b:4:2.english: They suspend - If they are terumah.

Rashi on Niddah 2b:4:3.english: And they do not burn - As is taught in the baraita of "One who sees a stain" later in our chapter (Niddah 6a).

Rashi on Niddah 2b:4:4.english: Whereas here - In [the case of] the ritual bath.

Rashi on Niddah 2b:4:5.hebrew: טומאה ודאית - מטמאינן להו למפרע, ושורפין את התרומה, מדקתני בר"ה טמא, אלמא כודאי משוי ליה:
Rashi on Niddah 2b:4:5.english: Definite impurity - We deem them impure retroactively and burn the terumah, since [the mishna] teaches that in the public domain [they are] impure; evidently, it treats it as a certainty.

Rashi on Niddah 2b:5:1.hebrew: לא טבל - טבילה הוגנת, הלכך טומאה ודאית יש:
Rashi on Niddah 2b:5:1.english: He did not immerse - [With] a proper immersion; therefore, there is definite ritual impurity.

Rashi on Niddah 2b:7:1.hebrew: חסר ואתא חסר ואתא - ואיתרע לה לחזקה מקמי הכי טובא, ולא ידעינן מאימת, הלכך ריע טפי מאשה:
Rashi on Niddah 2b:7:1.english: It continually diminished, continually diminished - And its presumption was impaired well before this, and we do not know from when; therefore, it is more impaired than [that of] a woman.

Rashi on Niddah 2b:7:2.hebrew: הכא מי איכא למימר כו' - הלכך, עד שעת מציאת דם לא איתרעי חזקה, והך דאישתכח השתא איכא למימר דהשתא הוא דחזאי:
Rashi on Niddah 2b:7:2.english: Here, can it be said, etc. - Therefore, until the time the blood was found, the presumption [of purity] was not impaired, and regarding this [blood] that was found now, it can be said that it is [only] now that she saw [it].

Rashi on Niddah 2b:7:3.hebrew: הגס הגס - לשון רבייה, שהדם הולך וגדל. ודומה לו במסכת שביעית בפ"ד: בראשונה היו אומרים מלקט אדם מתוך שדהו עצים ועשבים הגס הגס כדרך שמלקט משל חבירו, כו'. כלומר, ע"י שיהיה הדם רבה במקור, יוצא ממנו מעט מעט כחרדל מה שאין המקור יכול להחזיקה, ויוצא מעט לבית החיצון, וזה כמה ימים התחיל, והיא נטמאת מטיפת דם כחרדל, כדלקמן (נדה דף מ.):
Rashi on Niddah 2b:7:3.english: The larger, the larger - An expression of increase, that the blood progressively grows [in volume]. And similar to it is in Tractate Shevi'it, in chapter 4: "Initially they would say: A person may gather wood and grass from within his field, the larger [pieces], just as he gathers from that of his fellow," etc. That is to say: because the blood increases in the uterus, that which the uterus cannot contain issues from it little by little, [in drops the size of] a mustard seed, and a small amount goes out into the outer chamber. And this began several days ago, and she became ritually impure from a drop of blood [the size of] a mustard seed, as [stated] later (Niddah 40a).

Rashi on Niddah 2b:8:1.hebrew: תרתי לריעותא - העמד טמא על חזקת טומאה, ובחזקת טהרה דמקוה איכא ריעותא, שהרי חסר לפניך. אבל באשה, בדידה הוא דאיכא ריעותא, שהורע חזקת טהרתה קצת, שהרי דם לפניך; ומשום הך ריעותא לחודה לא מרעינן לה, הואיל ובטהרות לא משכחת ריעותא אחריתא, דכי אמרת: העמידם על חזקתם - בחזקת טהרתם הם:
Rashi on Niddah 2b:8:1.english: Two [factors] of impairment - Establish the impure [person] upon [his] presumption of impurity, and in the presumption of purity of the mikveh there is an impairment, as behold, it is deficient before you. However, regarding a woman, it is in her [alone] that there is an impairment, for the presumption of her ritual purity has been somewhat weakened, as behold, blood is before you; and on account of this impairment alone we do not impair her [status], since in the ritually pure items [she handled] you do not find another impairment, for when you say: "Establish them upon their presumption" — they are in their presumption of purity.

Rashi on Niddah 2b:9:1.english: And how is it different from a barrel - [The Gemara] poses the objection against Beit Shammai.

Rashi on Niddah 2b:9:2.english: [If] one was checking the barrel - Tasting it [to see] if it is in its presumptive state, that it has not turned sour.

Rashi on Niddah 2b:9:3.hebrew: להיות מפריש עליה - כלומר, להיות סומך עליה, והולך ושותה שאר חביות, ונותן עיניו בזו להפריש ממנה עליהם לאחר זמן, שהתרומה ניטלת במחשבה:
Rashi on Niddah 2b:9:3.english: To be separating upon it - That is to say, to rely upon it and go ahead and drink [from] the other barrels, and set his eyes on this [barrel] to separate from it for them at a later time, since terumah is taken through thought.

Rashi on Niddah 2b:9:4.hebrew: כל ג' ימים ודאי - פלוגתא דר' יוחנן ור' יהושע בן לוי בבבא בתרא בפ' המוכר פירות (בבא בתרא דף צו.). ר' יוחנן אומר: כל ג' ימים לאחר בדיקה ראשונה שמצאה בחזקתה — ודאי יין; ואם אמר בתוך ג' ימים: "הרי זו תרומה על אלו הסמוכין לה" — כולם מתוקנות. מכאן ואילך — ספק, ותרומה היא, ויחזור ויתרום. ור' יהושע בן לוי אומר: כל ג' ימים קודם בדיקה אחרונה שנמצאת חומץ — ודאי חומץ, דכיון דעכשיו חומץ גמור הוא, ודאי אין פחות מג' ימים שהתחיל להחמיץ; ואם עשאו בתוך אותן ג' ימים תרומה על מקום אחר — אינו תרומה, אליבא דרבי, דאמר בהמוכר את הספינה (ב ב פד:): "יין וחומץ שני מינין הן"; דאי לרבנן, הא קיימא לן (תרומות פ"ב מ"ו): תרם מן הרעה על היפה תרומתו תרומה. מכאן ואילך למפרע — ספק, והויא זו תרומה, ויחזור ויתרום. אלמא, בין למר בין למר מספקינן ריעותא למפרע:
Rashi on Niddah 2b:9:4.english: All three days [it is] definite - [This is] a dispute between Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi in Bava Batra in the chapter "HaMocher Peirot" (Bava Batra 96a). Rabbi Yochanan says: All three days after the first inspection in which he found it in its [presumed] status, [it is] definitely wine; and if he said within [those] three days, "This is hereby terumah for those [barrels] that rely upon it," they are all rectified. From then on, [it is in] doubt: it is [treated as] terumah, but he must go back and separate terumah [again]. And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says: All three days prior to the final inspection in which it was found [to be] vinegar, [it is] definitely vinegar, because since it is now complete vinegar, it is certainly not less than three days since it began to turn into vinegar; and if he made it terumah during those three days for [wine in] another place, it is not terumah, according to Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], who said in "HaMocher Et HaSefina" (Bava Batra 84b): "Wine and vinegar are two [distinct] species"; for if [it were] according to the Rabbis, behold we maintain (Terumot 2:6): "If one separated terumah from poor-quality [produce] for good-quality [produce], his terumah is [valid] terumah." From then on retroactively, [it is in] doubt: this is [treated as] terumah, but he must go back and separate terumah [again]. Evidently, whether according to the one Master or according to the other Master, we hold the deterioration in doubt retroactively.

Tosafot on Niddah 2b:1:1.hebrew: דאיכא ריעותא מגופה - אבל אי לאו האי טעמא, הוה מוקמינן לה אחזקת טהרה, אע"ג דהשתא ודאי טמאה; כמו בנגע באחד, דמטהרים אף רבנן בראהו חי מבערב, אע"ג דהשתא הוא מת וליכא עוד חזקת חיות. [והא דאמרי' פ"ק דחולין (דף ט.) גבי בא זאב ונטל בני מעיים, התם גמרינן מסוטה דבר"ה ספיקו טהור, היינו לפי סברת דברי המקשה, דמדמי איסור לסכנתא; אבל מסקנא, דשני לן בין איסורא לסכנתא, לא ילפי' מסוטה. גי'] ומ"מ, אם עשו מבהמה גבינות ושחטוה ונמצאת טרפה, אין להתיר הגבינות מטעם אוקי בהמ' בחזק' שלא היתה טרפה מתחלה; כיון דמעולם לא היתה אותה שעה מבוררת, לא חשיבה חזקה, כדמוכח בהכל שוחטין (חולין יא:), דקאמר: אתיא ממכה אביו ומפרה אדומה דאזלינן בתר רובא. והיכי מוכח? דלמא משום דמוקי לה בחזקת שאינה טרפה! אלא, לא חשיב אותה חזקה כדפרישית; וצ"ע להתיר הגבינות:
Tosafot on Niddah 2b:1:1.english: For there is an impairment from her body - However, were it not for this reason, we would establish her on [her] presumption of purity, even though now she is definitely impure; just as in [the case of one who] touched one [of two people, one living and one dead], where even the Rabbis declare [him] pure if he saw him alive the previous evening, even though now he is dead and there is no longer a presumption of life. [And that which we say in the first chapter of Chullin (folio 9a) regarding [the case where] a wolf came and took the intestines, that there we derive from sotah that in the public domain its uncertainty is pure — that is according to the reasoning of the questioner's words, who equates prohibition to danger; but according to the conclusion, where we distinguish between prohibition and danger, we do not derive from sotah. Gloss.] And nevertheless, if they made cheeses from an animal, and [subsequently] slaughtered it and it was found to be a tereifah, one cannot permit the cheeses on the grounds of: "Establish the animal on its presumption that it was not a tereifah initially"; since that time was never clearly verified, it is not considered a [valid] presumption, as is proven in [the chapter] "Hakol Shochtin" (Chullin 11b), where [the Gemara] says: It is derived from "one who strikes his father" and from the red heifer that we follow the majority. And how is it proven [from there]? Perhaps [it is permitted] because one establishes it on the presumption that it is not a tereifah! Rather, that presumption is not considered [valid], as I explained; and [therefore] permitting the cheeses requires further study.

Tosafot on Niddah 2b:4:1.hebrew: להלל קשה ודאי - דמדקאמר ר' שמעון בסיפא ברה"י תולין, מכלל דטמאות דקאמרי רבנן ברישא היינו ודאי:
Tosafot on Niddah 2b:4:1.english: For Hillel, [there is] a difficulty [regarding] definite [impurity] - For from [the fact] that Rabbi Shimon states in the latter clause, "In a private domain [they] suspend," by inference, [the ruling of] "impure" that the Rabbis state in the first clause means definite [impurity].

Tosafot on Niddah 2b:6:1.hebrew: השתא הוא דחזאי - ורב דאמר בפ' י' יוחסין (קידושין עט.) הרי היא בוגרת לפנינו, גבי קדשה אבי' בדרך וקדשה עצמה בעיר, ושניהם ביומא דמשלים ו' חדשים שבין נערות לבגרות, ולא קאמר השתא הוא דבגרה — היינו משום דרגילות שערות לבא מצפרא. וכי פריך התם לשמואל ממקוה וחבית, ה"נ מצי למיפרך לרב, דדוקא בשערות קאמר רב? אלא דפריך לשמואל טפי בפשיטות. והא דקאמר התם: לימא רב דאמר כר' נתן, דאמר אם בריא הוא עליו להביא ראיה ששכיב מרע היה — אע"ג דרב דוקא בשערות קאמר, התם נמי רוב העולם בריאים, ואית לן למימר דבריא היה כמו שהוא עכשיו:
Tosafot on Niddah 2b:6:1.english: It is [only] now that she saw - And [as for] Rav, who said in the chapter "Asarah Yuchasin" (Kiddushin 79a), "She is a grown woman (bogeret) before us," regarding [the case where] her father betrothed her on the road and she betrothed herself in town, and both [betrothals occurred] on the day that completes the six months between maidenhood (na'arut) and adulthood (bagrut), and he did not say, "It is [only] now that she matured" — that is because it is common for [pubic] hairs to appear in the morning. And when it raised an objection there against Shmuel from [the cases of] a mikveh and a barrel, could it not also have objected against Rav, [or was it because] Rav spoke specifically regarding hairs? Rather, it objected against Shmuel [because that was] more straightforward. And as for that which it says there, "Shall we say Rav spoke in accordance with Rabbi Natan, who said: If he is [currently] healthy, the burden of proof is upon him to bring evidence that he was on his deathbed (shekhiv mera)?" — even though Rav spoke specifically regarding hairs, there too the majority of people are healthy, and we have [grounds] to say that he was healthy [earlier] just as he is now.

Tosafot on Niddah 2b:8:1.hebrew: התם תרתי לריעותא - תימה, דבפ"ק דחולין (דף י. ושם) אמרינן: שחטה ונמצא הסכין פגום ושבר בו עצמות אחרי כן, רב חסדא אמר כשרה, משום דעצם ודאי פוגם, כו'. ופריך ליה: מטבל ועלה ונמצא עליו דבר חוצץ, אע"פ שנתעסק באותו המין כל היום כולו — לא עלתה לו טבילה. ומשני: סכין איתרעי, בהמה לא איתרעי. והשתא, הא איכא תרתי לריעותא: דהרי פגום לפניך, והעמד בהמה בחזקת איסור, כדאמר הכא; דה"נ איתרעי מקוה ואדם לא איתרעי, ואפ"ה מטמאינן! וי"ל, דהתם משום דעצם ודאי פוגם, כדאמר התם. א"נ, אין סברא לחלק בין מקוה איתרעי לאדם איתרעי, והתם ה"פ: סכין איתרעי — ואיכא ספיקי טובא: שמא בעצם נפגם; ואפי' בעור נפגם — שמא נפגם במיעוט בתרא; ואת"ל נפגם במיעוט קמא — שמא לא שחט כנגד הפגימה. אך קשה, דאמר התם: מנלן דאזלינן בתר חזקה? דכתיב: "ויצא הכהן מן הבית" — ודילמא אדנפיק ואתי בציר ליה שיעורא? אלא אוקמי' אחזקה. וקשה: התם משום דליכא ריעותא, ואכתי היכא דאיכא ריעותא, מנלן דאזלינן בתר חזקה? וי"ל, דמוכח היכא דבא כהן בסוף שבוע וראה והנה כהה הנגע ואיתרע חזקה, מטמאינן אדם הנכנס שם באותו שבוע, וחייב קרבן אם נכנס בעזרה. וקשה: אדרבה, נימא התם הרי חסר הנגע לפניך, ואוקי גברא בחזקת טהרה, כדאמר הכא גבי מקוה לטמא בודאי? וי"ל, דגבי מקוה רגילות להתחסר מעט מעט, ולכך איכא למימר דמעיקרא חסר; אבל הנגע רגילות להתחסר בבת אחת פחות מכגריס, לכך אמרינן התם: השתא הוא דחסר, ואוקי הנגע בחזקת שלם ביציאת כהן מן הבית. וכשטימא הכהן את הבית, אפי' נתחסר הנגע אחרי כן קודם שנכנס זה — גזירת הכתוב הוא שהבית טמא, עד שיראה הכהן בסוף שבוע ויטהרנו:
Tosafot on Niddah 2b:8:1.english: There, there are two adverse factors - It is astounding! For in the first chapter of Chullin (folio 10a and there), we say: If one slaughtered [an animal] and the knife was found notched, and he broke bones with it afterwards, Rav Chisda said: It is kosher, because a bone definitely notches [a blade], etc. And [the Gemara] challenges him from: [If one] immersed and came up, and an intervening substance (chatzitzah) was found upon him, even though he had been engaged with that [same] substance all day long, his immersion has not counted for him. And [the Gemara] answers: The knife suffered an impairment, [but] the animal did not suffer an impairment. And now, behold there are two adverse factors: for behold, [the knife] is notched before you, and establish the animal on its presumption of prohibition [as a live animal is forbidden until validly slaughtered], just as it says here; for here too, the mikveh suffered an impairment, and the person did not suffer an impairment, and even so we deem [him] impure! And one can say that there [in Chullin], it is because a bone definitely notches [the blade], as [the Gemara] says there. Alternatively, it is not reasonable to distinguish between "the mikveh suffered an impairment" and "the person suffered an impairment" [or the knife and animal]; and there, this is what it means: "The knife suffered an impairment" — and there are many doubts: perhaps it was notched on the bone; and even if it was notched on the hide, perhaps it was notched during the final minority [of the slaughter, after the majority of the neck organs were already severed]; and if you should say it was notched during the initial minority, perhaps he did not slaughter against the notch [with that part of the blade]. However, it is difficult: For [the Gemara] says there: From where do we derive that we follow a presumption (chazakah)? As it is written: "And the priest shall go out of the house" (Leviticus 14:38) — and perhaps while he was going out and coming, its measurement diminished? Rather, establish it on its presumption! And this is difficult: There, it is because there is no adverse factor [at hand]; but where there is an adverse factor, from where do we derive that we follow a presumption? And one can say that it is proven from [the case] where the priest came at the end of the week and saw that behold, the affliction had dimmed, and [thus] the presumption was impaired, [and yet] we deem impure a person who entered there during that week, and he is liable to [bring] a sacrifice if he entered the [Temple] Courtyard (Azarah). And it is difficult: On the contrary! Let us say there: "Behold, the affliction is diminished before you, and establish the person on his presumption of purity" — just as it says here regarding the mikveh, to rule [him] definitely impure?! And one can say that regarding a mikveh, it is customary [for the water] to diminish little by little, and therefore it can be said that it was deficient from the outset; but an affliction usually diminishes all at once to less than [the size of] a split-bean (kigris). Therefore, we say there: "It is only now that it diminished," and establish the affliction on its presumption of being complete at the time of the priest's departure from the house. And once the priest rendered the house impure [by quarantining it], even if the affliction diminished afterwards before this [person] entered, it is a scriptural decree that the house is impure until the priest inspects [it] at the end of the week and purifies it.

Tosafot on Niddah 2b:9:1.hebrew: היה בודק את החבית - אפי' לרבנן דאית להו בהמוכר את הספינה (ב"ב פד.) יין וחומץ מין אחד הוא, היינו כשמתכוין לתרום מן החומץ; והכא מיירי שנתכוין לתרום מן היין ונמצא חומץ, דהוה ליה תרומה בטעות, כדמשמע בתוספתא דתרומות פרק התודה והמעשר:
Tosafot on Niddah 2b:9:1.english: [If] one was checking the barrel - Even according to the Rabbis, who hold in [the chapter] "HaMokher Et HaSefinah" (Bava Batra 84b) that wine and vinegar are one species, that is [only] when he intends to separate [terumah] from the vinegar; but here we are dealing with [a case where] he intended to separate from the wine, and it was found [to be] vinegar, for it is [then] an erroneous separation of terumah (terumah be-ta'ut), as is implied in the Tosefta of Terumot, chapter "HaToda VeHaMa'aser".
